key_insight: An image-based deep learning system can classify emergency ECGs from photos, scans, and PDFs with performance close to cardiologists.
clinical_relevance: This could help emergency workflows when digital ECG waveforms are unavailable, especially for digitized or photographed tracings.
method: Trained a ConvNeXt ensemble on the InCor-EMG dataset of 18,519 expert-adjudicated emergency ECG images.
Evaluated 12 ECG categories using a held-out test set and compared performance with cardiologists and a commercial ECG interpretation system.
Tested robustness on scanned, photographed, temporal, and heterogeneous public-image settings.
evidence_signal: On the held-out test set, the final ConvNeXt ensemble reached macro F1 0.807, versus 0.820 for annotating cardiologists, and outperformed Mortara Veritas in most categories.
watch_item: Performance depends on image quality and category agreement, so real-world deployment should account for variable acquisition conditions and local validation.
paper_title: Image-based deep learning for emergency electrocardiogram classification
